takeaways: Targets need at least 24×24 CSS px. 44×44 — 2.5.5, Level AAA — is the comfortable goal.
Spacing exception: a smaller target passes if a 24px circle centered on it doesn’t touch another target or another small target’s circle.
Links inside sentences are exempt, as are targets whose size is set by the browser.
The hit area can be bigger than the visible icon. Pad the glyph; don’t scale it.
failures: Dense toolbars of 16px icons touching each other
A tiny × to close a modal
check: Overlay a 24×24 square on every target in your file.
For small targets, draw 24px circles at their centers — do any overlap?
Annotate hit areas at handoff so developers build them.

quiz.question: A 20×20 icon button sits 20px away from the nearest other button. Does it pass?
quiz.why: A 24px circle centered on it doesn’t reach its neighbor, so the spacing exception applies. Still — bigger is kinder.

spec: Draw the hit area as its own annotated layer, with its size in px.
Note the minimum spacing between neighboring targets.
Call out anything under 24px and the exception it relies on.
review: Where is the smallest target on this screen, and who has to hit it?
Are dense areas such as tables and toolbars leaning on the spacing exception?
Is the hit area specified, or only the icon?
tradeoff: Density against reach. Keep the visual density if you must. Grow the invisible hit area and the spacing, not the glyphs.
system: Set a minimum hit area on the base button and icon button: a 24px floor, 44px by default on touch.
pitch: A missed tap is an error, a retry or an abandoned task. That is true for anyone on a moving train, not only people with tremors.
